visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final portable views including the curated 1024×640 preview. Individual Imam Husayn shrine has a pointed golden bulb on blue drum, two mapped cylindrical gold minarets with broad balconies and smaller upper caps, a five-bay gold-columned pointed portico, covered central court/gallery, ten mapped gate ranges, shallow roof caps and Qibla upper clock stage. Added inward outer-wall skin and the missing covered-roof underside, then moved the portico camera below that roof before final review. Dome and shafts remain deliberately faceted at medium-fi scale. Portable grazing shadow striping remains visible around the portico bands. Fine inscriptions, faience artwork, festival lighting, flags, crowds, chandeliers, crypts and furnished interiors are omitted.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 11 shared-material/geographic-flat views, including the placement overlay. Six existing shared 256² stucco, raw limestone, lime plaster, marble, cast bronze and mosaic graphs serve seven merged roles including local opaque blue-grey fields. Metric UVs, linear colors and no embedded images or copied photographs. All graphs are read once; unloading leaves zero model geometries and restores ground. Retained reference anchor is fixed; exact current core edge supplies the axis. Main gallery cutout follows its raw outer outline. Ten separately mapped gate roofs retain their native outlines and small quantization gaps, with their own foundations; the model does not invent a connected city-wide footprint. Flat ground verifies transform, material reuse and replacement, not actual grade.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 27 final medium-fi frames: Economy/High, noon/late light, three distances, untextured silhouette, six details, four matched LODs and four transitions. The matched skyline was also inspected at full size. Skyline 826 triangles retains all gate masses, covered gallery, main gold dome, two minaret silhouettes, low roof caps and Qibla upper stage, but drops facade fields, railings and rooflights. District 3697 restores sparse lower facade fields, blue drum bands and more curved caps. Street 13828 restores two-level fields, rooflights and balcony rails with fewer bays and simple inner door/window panes. Closeup 43824 adds denser facade rhythm, inner gallery fields and detailed pointed surrounds. Initial skyline plus district is 476112 bytes plus shared textures, one/seven draws. Sparse far roof caps and facade density visibly change between levels; static transition shots and synthetic neighbors do not establish full-city frame rate. Physical phone/tablet/laptop timings remain pending.

fidelityReview.notes: Individual medium-fi Imam Husayn shrine: mapped covered gallery and central core, golden pointed bulb dome on blue drum, two tall golden balcony minarets, gold-columned front portico, ten mapped gate ranges, Qibla gate upper clock stage and repeated shallow courtyard roof caps. Coarse blue faience fields and pale stone surfaces use six existing shared 256² graphs across seven merged roles. Four independent browser LODs. Component centers and total map heights are controlled; internal profiles, bays, facade facing, rooflights and ornament are explicit visualization estimates. Separate expansion, fine calligraphy/artwork, furnishings, crypts, festivals and city omitted. Current map: gallery 12.5 m, core 12 m, golden dome 32 m with min_height 12 m, minaret balconies 34–34.5 m and upper minaret parts 34.5–44 m. Gate roofs 11.3 m; small roof caps 14.5 m; Qibla gate upper square 17.3 m and octagonal upper control 21.3 m. Total heights are honored. Internal picture-led estimates: main blue drum 12–17 m, golden bulb to 31.4 m and finial to 32 m; gold shafts to 32.5 m, projecting balcony to 34.5 m, slender upper stage to 40 m, cap/finial to 44 m. Covered-court rooflights, entrance arch divisions, dome/minaret curves, gold portico spacing and clock divisions are estimates. Coarse map heights do not establish those internal levels. No surveyed engineering or furnished interior claim. Two actually inspected pictures guide the golden portico, dome/minaret silhouettes and covered-court material rhythm. An earlier night exterior shows an open court; the supplementary picture shows a covered courtyard with rooflights. The model follows current roofed map geometry without claiming a precise historical snapshot. The first photograph has uncertain original provenance and conflicting title/date metadata; the second has an unreliable default-looking EXIF date. Photographs are viewed only. Current total height and upper-part tags are honored, but internal profiles, facade facing, bay counts, rooflight locations and exact clock structure remain estimates. Orientation uncertainty is recorded as 30 degrees; no surveyed engineering, furnished or collision-certified interior claim. Exact finishes, hidden rooms and physical-device timings remain unverified.
